newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices drop in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices drop in thin trade.

text.p: Prices fell on Istanbul's gold exchange in line with European markets, dealers said on Thursday.
Volume remained low due to slack public demand.
Gold closed at 1,096,250 lira per gram and $382.95 an ounce, down 2,750 lira and $0.85 from Wednesday.
"Trade was dull and dominated by sellers today," said one dealer, adding that uncertainty over the future direction of gold in international markets further discouraged market players.
Free market dealers said public demand for gold remained weak as the active summer season was about to end.
An influx of tourists buoys demand for gold jewellery while gold coins and jewellery are given as traditional gifts in weddings and other ceremonies which show a rise during the summer.
Volume shrank to 75 kilos in the second session from 497 in the morning.
Of total trade, 85 percent was in lira terms, reflecting currency weakness. The lira closed at 89,030 to the dollar, down from 88,835 on Wednesday.
